主要内容: Andreessen Horowitz, a prominent venture capital firm based in Menlo Park, has made a historic philanthropic pledge. All six partners at the firm have committed to donating at least half of their lifetime income from venture capital investments to charity. This marks the first time an entire VC firm has made such a pledge. Founding Partner Marc Andreessen hopes this will set an example for other private equity and venture capital funds. His partner, Ben Horowitz, noted that if the firm meets its goals of being a top-tier VC firm, this could mean billions of dollars for charity. The firm has backed over 100 companies, including Facebook, Groupon, Twitter, Zynga, Foursquare, and Instagram. It has raised a total of $2.7 billion since 2009 and has already returned the principal of its first $200 million fund to investors after just three years. The decision was influenced by the firm's culture, with partner Scott Weiss suggesting the idea during his interview for the role.
